description: Exact-source two-process compatibility drill proving that a pinned historical candidate and current Import API can mutate, replay, concurrently contend for and safely recover an interrupted persisted Apply idempotency claim on one current expanded PostgreSQL schema. The candidate remains explicitly non-release evidence.
requiredScenarios: current-issued session invokes historical candidate Apply for Preview A
current process replays the exact historical-candidate idempotency claim for Preview A
historical-candidate-issued session invokes current Apply for Preview B
historical candidate replays the exact current idempotency claim for Preview B
reusing Preview A idempotency key for Preview B is rejected as conflict
sequential scenarios leave exactly two applied claims and two memory items with no in-progress claim
historical candidate and current process simultaneously Apply Preview C with one idempotency key and converge on one Apply ID with one first application and one replay
after the concurrent race exactly three applied claims, three memory items and three source Previews remain with one claim and one memory item for Preview C and zero in-progress claims
a test-only advisory-lock boundary proves historical Apply for Preview D is inside its PostgreSQL transaction before memory materialization and the historical process is then SIGKILLed
the killed historical transaction leaves zero Apply claims, zero memory items and zero in-progress residue for Preview D
the current process accepts the same historical-issued session, Preview D and idempotency key after process death and creates exactly one durable claim and memory item
after recovery exactly four applied claims, four memory items and four distinct source Previews remain with zero in-progress claims
abortCriteria: old backend is not the pinned full SHA or is not an ancestor of current source
either process fails to build or become healthy
current migration sequence cannot apply cleanly
synthetic Preview cannot be committed through the current Preview committer
either first Apply fails to create exactly one memory item
either opposite process cannot replay the original Apply ID
same idempotency key can be reused for another Preview
simultaneous old/current claims do not both return success after contention
concurrent claims do not split into exactly one first application and one replay
concurrent claims return different Apply IDs or materialize more than one memory item
historical Apply does not reach the observed blocked in-transaction boundary before process termination
the killed historical transaction leaves any Apply claim, memory item or in-progress residue
current recovery of the exact historical request does not create exactly one durable claim and memory item
any Apply claim remains in progress
result would contain a token, database URL, account, job, Preview or idempotency identifier
limitations: historical candidate is not an approved predecessor release
one simultaneous old/current claim race only
one historical-process SIGKILL at a test-only advisory-lock boundary before memory materialization
no host failure, network partition or production connection pool
no rolling traffic drain or application rollback
no destructive contract migration or downgrade
